Yes — under those conditions, you would very likely be able to spot the Moon.

At 21.1° above the horizon, it is comfortably above most local obstructions if you have a reasonably open view toward the southwest (azimuth about 239°, roughly west-southwest). A 37%-illuminated Moon is a fairly conspicuous crescent/gibbous-looking partial Moon, and with a clear nighttime sky it is easily visible to normal unaided eyesight.

Its 75° separation from the Sun is irrelevant to glare at that time because the Sun is nearly 50° below the horizon. The Moon’s distance is also normal and does not make it unusually faint.

The main things that could prevent you from seeing it would be practical rather than astronomical: buildings, trees, hills, haze near the horizon, bright nearby lights, or looking in the wrong part of the sky. But if you can see the southwest sky about 20° up — roughly two fist-widths held at arm’s length above the horizon — it should be visible.
